experiences.text: Dismiss nitpicks about hardcoded regex lists or synchronization hazards during bug fixes.

EMPHASIZE PRA-POSSIBLE_BUG only when you trace a concrete, reproducible silent-failure path (e.g., vars.TOUCHSTONE_TAXONOMY_TYPES being passed through unmerged so one label shrinks the vocab and fail-closed drops every standard type, or an empty-set taxonomy silently decoupling from enforce and wasting a whole distillation run) — skip speculative 'if a cache might exist' hypotheses.

Re-run pip-audit on the final locked venv that actually ships in the release and record the dated result as evidence, since the changelog's 'zero known vulnerabilities' claim only holds for the selection-time dependency tree.
Do not speculate about hardcoded threshold values needing configurability or significance testing unless the repo already uses such patterns.

Don't add speculative scope-broadeners like exempting test-file globs from applies_to:"*" without a demonstrated false positive; this appeared only in the lowest-reward review and humans dismissed it.
Skip hypothetical-future-miss security arguments (a future L1 leak still posts tags); threat models not demonstrated by this diff are dismissed by reviewers here.
Replace hardcoded indentation constants in CommonMark rendering with dynamic calculation to prevent future regressions.
Flag only concrete, verifiable defects in the new failure path — e.g. raise without `from e` losing the HTTP status and Retry-After — since maintainers act on specific mechanical fixes.

EMPHASIZE PRA-REVIEW findings that attack the mechanism itself with a concrete remedy and a test (soft 'MUST be one of' prompts can't stop hallucinated types — make score_review clamp out-of-vocab output and add an enforce-on end-to-end no-all-negative-reward assertion; put PRA-REVIEW into the label vocab or derive the whitelist from raised/adopted signals instead of per-env var comments) rather than framing it as test-intent or coverage nitpicks.

Keep PRA-MAINTAINABILITY suppressed for data chores — the repo's own experience store carries multi-PR evidence for this suppression, and idempotency/reproducibility lectures in these -3.5/-4.0 reviews were ignored.

Do not raise expression-injection findings for trusted first-party setup-python outputs; humans dismiss this as hygiene on CI scripts, and if mentioned at all it belongs as one line inside the design note.
Prioritize verifying the exact semantic behavior of edge cases like the '0' value to ensure it disables the limit as intended.
Confirm that the downstream consumer code correctly parses the new variable states defined in the workflow configuration.
Do not spend a finding on stderr-redirect polish or comment trimming; humans dismiss style nitpicks on a working CI hotfix.
Do not request documentation updates for internal CI variable wiring changes.
Do not request removal of historical context from inline comments that explain the rationale for the change.

Emphasize anti-drift test gaps in this repo's doc-sync suite: require a negative assertion that the retired phrase 「每 2 分钟」 is absent and fold README into test_skill_doc_sync, since reviewers immediately merge concrete copy-pasteable assertion fixes.
Highlight concrete logic discrepancies, such as function signature mismatches between test suites and their corresponding implementations.
Ignore warnings about missing implementation updates if the codebase likely expects partial changes across multiple files.
Omit speculative robustness concerns about truncated marker payloads leaking content unless a concrete leak path is shown in the code.
Dismiss logic findings concerning trivial discrepancies between code comments and test assertions, such as off-by-one counts for line breaks.
Dismiss feedback regarding brittle implementation checks in tests when behavioral verification is sufficient.
Do not flag technical implementation details in documentation history tables as redundant.
Dismiss suggestions to replace print statements with the logging module in fix commits.
Suppress speculative architectural critiques about hardcoded regex patterns or maintenance risks for newly implemented invariant gates.
Suppress speculative SSRF-bypass constructions about whitelist exemption code that is not part of this diff — invented threat scenarios humans won't act on in a release-notes PR.
Skip test-hygiene nitpicks such as import placement inside test functions or rewriting inspect.getsource sentinels as pure-function round-trip tests — humans dismiss these on small PRs.
Drop the 'best_practices.md is generated output, regenerate or don't hand-edit' framing; higher-reward reviewers accepted the hand edit and routed consistency concerns to test assertions instead.
Critique the technical validity of the proposed logic (such as regex side effects on formatting) described in the changelog.
Dismiss feedback regarding high coupling between tests and prompt templates, as this is often intentional for integration validation.
Do not flag tests that verify internal implementation details or source code content as problematic.
Ignore suggestions to refactor test utilities or extract mocks into shared fixtures.
Identify when generic utilities are defined in domain-specific modules, causing unnecessary coupling.
Dismiss nitpicks regarding code style and readability in favor of functional correctness.
Raise the version-drift point under PRA-DOC as the top-reward review did rather than a generic maintainability label, keeping this repo's findings concentrated in CI/SEC/TEST/BUG/DOC.
Identify test brittleness arising from hardcoded HTML fragments or string splitting on volatile content.
Flag excessive narrative history and issue tracking numbers within inline comments or docstrings.
Dismiss minor style critiques regarding f-string concatenation or specific string formatting choices.
Avoid reporting on inconsistencies in whitespace or line break handling within HTML rendering logic.
Suppress feedback on test implementation details such as manual tag counting when functional testing is maintained.

Keep PRA-ROBUSTNESS findings tied to concrete present fragility, such as guarding the unguarded frag.split with an assert and documenting the implicit three-prose-line fixture contract behind the
==2 check.
Verify API response structures to avoid silently skipping files when encountering unexpected data formats.
Prioritize explicit configuration checks over implicit string matching to prevent false positive platform detection.
Replace deprecated functions with portable, future-proof standard library alternatives.
Avoid compatibility speculation about unknown consumers of the (diff, any_ok) tuple contract; the actionable core is syncing tests to the new contract and asserting exit codes.
Do not report potential TypeErrors from deserializing legacy JSON markers when fields are removed from state dataclasses.

Treat truncated 310-to-11 diffs as unreviewable and require a machine-generated manifest (removed id mapped to rejection reason), the survivor list with evidence, and confirmation that no locked entries were purged.
Do not challenge the classification of deleted entries as hallucinations based on standard taxonomy values.
Drop soft-retire-vs-hard-delete and version-bump design counsel on data cleanses — migration-style design advice is dismissed on single-commit chore PRs.
Verify that test files referencing new logic are accompanied by the corresponding implementation in the source code.
Identify and correct obvious factual errors in comments, such as invalid future dates.
Suggest replacing manual configuration steps described in workflow comments with automated logic to prevent operator error.
Avoid inferring strict operational requirements or race conditions from test docstrings without confirming the implementation details.
Do not speculate about internal implementation requirements, such as sorting cache keys, based solely on test assertions.
Refrain from drawing conclusions about architectural limitations or user impact for custom functions based exclusively on unit test mock setups.
Do not repackage the len(frag) cap issue as PRA-TEST-ROBUSTNESS with 'unbounded monotonic failure' framing; the concrete math-check NIT version is what lands, the abstraction is ignored.
Always verify that the diff is complete before flagging syntax errors or claiming implementation gaps.
Do not flag syntax errors that appear to be caused by truncated or incomplete diff boundaries.

Skip changelog style nits such as the [未发布] placeholder wording, internal PR-process details in the entry, and title dash/format alignment — the highest-reward review omits these entirely and humans do not act on them.
Prioritize findings that critique the statistical validity, decision thresholds, and maintenance automation of configuration updates.
Ignore findings flagging future-dated comments in snapshot files as these are likely intentional simulation placeholders.
Dismiss findings recommending the removal of hardcoded statistics from explanatory comments unless they cause parsing errors.
Do not request documentation updates for simple configuration downgrades or internal security fixes that do not change user-facing behavior.
Flag any discrepancy where the changelog lists new files or features that are completely absent from the provided diff.
Immediately block the review if security-critical scripts mentioned in the changelog are missing from the diff.
Do not raise issues regarding trivial metadata errors like future release dates when the diff lacks implementation code.
Skip docstring-wording corrections about what 'schema identical' claims mean; humans treat them as noise on a cap-removal diff.
Suppress resource leak warnings for short-lived read-only file operations in test utility functions.
Flag critical inconsistencies between the PR description and the diff when claimed code changes are missing.
Do not review specific workflow implementation details if the workflow files are absent from the diff.
Avoid generating configuration audit findings based solely on changelog text when the configuration files are missing.
Ensure that unexpected scanner exit codes trigger a hard failure rather than a neutral status to enforce a fail-closed security policy.
Warn that removing path exclusions for dependency directories will likely generate false positives that block valid development work.
Avoid suggesting automated updates for pinned security tool versions where stability and reproducibility are prioritized.
Skip raising hypothetical concerns about future JSON schema changes unless the current parsing logic is demonstrably fragile.
Do not request documentation enhancements or explanatory comments as critical findings during urgent workflow fixes.
Ensure that changes to detection logic are reflected in all related documentation and configuration hints to maintain cross-rule consistency.
Do not request additional test cases for minor edge patterns if the core logic implementation is correct.
Dismiss security warnings about `pull_request_target` usage for strictly read-only scanning jobs.
Suppress configuration findings questioning IP allowlists for private network ranges.

Suppress PRA-TEST requests for loader/schema validation of inert YAML seed files unless the reviewer demonstrates the file is actually wired into the prompt injector, as the lone such demand here rode in the -1-dismissed review.
Do not raise issues regarding missing source code diffs or refuse to review based solely on limited documentation changes.
Suppress open-ended design debates about persisting findings before the raise; humans dismiss 'consider writing the artifact first' musings that contradict the PR's stated intent.
Omit duplicate-comment spam warnings about repeated failure markers; reviewers themselves flag them as minor and humans dismiss them.
Do not flag signature changes in internal orchestrator components as breaking changes requiring version bumps or coordination.
Avoid criticizing hardcoded indentation values in template rendering logic as robustness issues.
Do not request audits of truncation logic to detect markdown structure boundaries or mid-string corruption.
Do not require explicit verification of call sites for internal refactors unless a specific bug is identified.
Do not flag inconsistencies between PR descriptions and diffs if the context provided is limited to documentation.
Verify that all referenced local files exist and links resolve correctly to prevent user-facing 404 errors.
Identify and flag obvious factual errors such as incorrect dates or contradictory information.
Suppress 'grep the codebase for consumers' and silent-reset warnings on data shrinks — authors dismiss consumer-impact speculation that cites no actual broken lookup.
Do not report missing implementation for release PRs that only contain changelog and version updates.
Avoid flagging hypothetical security or formatting risks based on variable interpolation or test names without concrete evidence of the defect in the code.
Verify that unit tests cover new logic such as signal adoption and seed parsing mechanisms.
Ignore minor skips in sequential version numbers unless they violate strict release management policies.
Prioritize identifying logic that allows PR changes to self-suppress security findings during the review process by reading from the working tree.
Do not report the use of `importlib.reload` in test fixtures as a reliability or race condition concern.
Dismiss warnings about shadowing built-ins when importing internal framework modules like `touchstone.re`.
Ensure that environment variables introduced in workflow files are synchronized with the corresponding constants in the codebase.
Remove redundant conditional checks in helper functions that are already guaranteed by the caller's logic.
Dismiss potential security risks from standard string splitting operations unless unsafe library calls are involved.
Do not flag log messages containing non-English characters as encoding issues if the repository context supports them.
Avoid flagging increased resource usage as a performance issue when the change intentionally expands the processing window.

Lead every stale-value fix with the root cause — import the fallback constant from pr_agent_runner.py instead of swapping one hardcoded literal (32768) for another (128000) that will silently drift again.

Lead with the unset-vs-empty trap: GitHub Secrets cannot store empty strings while Variables can, so verify every consumer of the migrated env vars treats unset and set-but-empty identically before endorsing the zero-behavior-change claim.

Run a repo-wide grep for the stale value '32768' — especially SECURITY.md and CHANGELOG.md, which the warning message itself cross-references — and fix all live occurrences in this same PR, leaving historical changelog entries untouched.

Report at most one or two structural coverage gaps visible in the diff (single-POST-site gating that other egress paths bypass, '-->' rewriting that mangles fenced code), since dense 11-finding reviews on this repo score negative while focused ones do not.

Avoid generic 'verify the claim at HEAD' bug-verify notes; fold any needed checks into PRA-VERIFY with concrete semantic depth (unset vs empty handling, provider-dependent defaults, exact quote matching).
Never spend a finding on no-action changelog confirmations ('structure matches, no action needed') — reviewers reward findings requiring work, not approvals.
Frame findings as cheap, checkable consistency questions on the changed files — SECURITY.md supported range, hardcoded 0.2.7 literals in tests/scripts, changelog date vs actual tag date.
Prioritize sharp catches inside the files actually changed, such as a README version example that is stale the moment this same release bumps __version__ past it.
Credit the clean release-prep structure and the explicit 'zero behavior change' parity note, since reviewers on this repo reward that transparency in release PRs.
Skip open-ended 'grep the repo for other call sites' risk notes; either verify the call sites and file a concrete PRA-TEST/PRA-BUG finding or omit it.
Stop demanding audit evidence (CI runs, #216 diffs) for the 'zero behavior change' claim — the best-received review simply accepted the explicit parity note.

Suppress proposals to add new CI drift-guards or release-automation checks in a metadata-only release PR — this suggestion appeared only in the worst review and reads as scope creep rather than feedback on the diff.
Avoid dumping merge-time chore lists (tag the commit, build smoke test, recheck SECURITY.md) — they duplicate question-framed checks and read as noise.

Stop relitigating patch-vs-minor bumps for additive artifact fields or demanding full field schemas on release PRs — maintainers dismiss versioning pedantry when the changelog already discloses the addition.
Drop wording audits of '契约零变化'-style claims that hinge on zero-change vs no-breaking-change distinctions; humans treat these as semantic quibbles on a release-only diff and ignore them.

Flag assertions that depend on text invisible in the diff (like the literal '## [未发布]' CHANGELOG heading) with a merge-blocking framing, since only the higher-reward reviews caught this and authors immediately go verify.

Verify that every changelog claim (PR-Agent 0.39.0→0.44.0 venv lock, new-field implementation, +10 cases, PR #208) actually exists in the commit that will be tagged, and grep the repo for stale hardcoded 0.3.1 strings in CI badges, SECURITY.md, release workflows, and Docker tag templates.
Don't request repo-wide dangling-reference sweeps for a deletion PR whose own tests already assert the removed content is absent.
Never flag possibly-unused imports as 'if' speculation on a pure-deletion PR—verify consumers with grep first or stay silent.
Do not complain that the implementation portion of the diff is truncated or invisible; humans dismiss process complaints rather than re-scope the PR.

Lead with the empty-string trap: since ${{ vars.TOUCHSTONE_MAX_DIFF_LINES }} renders '' (not unset) when unconfigured, verify _max_diff_lines uses a falsy-guard fallback rather than int(os.environ.get(NAME, 1000)), which raises ValueError on every run, and confirm this step's env actually reaches the process running the SIZE-001 gate.
Do not demand an audit of every sibling os.environ read in this PR; that scope expansion dilutes the review and gets ignored.
Do not propose CI schema validation, parse checks, or loader smoke tests for data-only changes — authors dismiss speculative validation infrastructure on chores with no code under test.
Skip demands to fix the ingestion pipeline or add canary/rollback plans on a one-off data cleanse — authors treat root-cause prevention as out of scope for a chore and penalize it.

Do not demand repopulation plans or before/after review-quality comparisons when a data store shrinks — this repo has long-learned suppression of PRA-COVERAGE and both negative-reward reviews confirm it is dismissed again here.

Suppress PRA-REVIEW findings that meta-critique calibration config like .touchstone/seeds.yaml — statistical-significance quibbles, feedback-loop and staleness speculation, comment-vs-structured-metadata demands, and unverifiable-snapshot complaints — since the only review carrying nine of them scored -1 while clean reviews scored 0.0, showing humans dismiss process speculation that is not a concrete defect.

On release PRs whose diff is only CHANGELOG plus the version bump, raise the changelog-vs-diff artifact reconciliation once as a concrete verification action (confirm each advertised file actually landed via its linked PR before tagging).
Emphasize verifiable arithmetic slips in budget comments (600→700 不等于 6×120=720) plus the pattern of repeatedly loosening the len(frag) cap, since exact-number NITs get fixed without debate.
Do not escalate the already-stated missing-artifact observation into BLOCKER/RELEASE severity or restate it under new finding types; one grounded confirmation request carries full weight.

When a release PR will be blocked by its own not-yet-active fail-closed gate, flag the chicken-and-egg immediately and force an explicit, documented merge path (admin override or recorded exemption) before tagging.
For version-bump release PRs whose diff is only CHANGELOG plus __version__, verify that every PR number cited in the release notes is actually merged to the release branch before approving.

Require in-repo evidence (regression tests actually running in CI, or the merged security PR) for any security-guarantee claim in release notes, because a changelog can assert protections that do not exist on the branch.
On every release bump, grep the repo for stale hardcoded version strings (SECURITY.md supported range, docs, lock files, CI badges) so only the dynamic source of __version__ needs editing.
Do not relitigate which existing changelog section falls under the new version heading; reviewers treat heading-placement pedantry on release PRs as noise.
Do not flag a missing Keep-a-Changelog compare linkref unless the repo demonstrably defines one for every prior version; it is cosmetic and dismissed.
Do not comment on the changelog date's format, timezone, or tag-day alignment; date-style nitpicks are ignored on version-bump PRs.

Reconcile every PR named in the release summary with a dedicated categorized entry (变更/修复) in the body — all four reviews converged on #218 being summary-only, making this the highest-confidence, definitely-acted-on finding on release PRs.

Whenever a new Keep-a-Changelog version heading is added, flag the required bottom-of-file compare-link definition ([0.3.7]: .../compare/v0.3.6...v0.3.7), since every review raised this dangling-reference risk and humans apply it as a mechanical, zero-risk fix.

Keep flagging literal placeholder prose under [未发布] as content that ships verbatim to readers and can break bullet-only release-note parsers — both top-reward reviews caught this and framed it concretely, so demand an HTML comment or an empty section.

On each version bump run a repo-wide grep for stale literal '0.3.6' in docs, SECURITY.md prose, badges, and pinned test snapshots, because the __version__ dynamic single-source claim leaves hardcoded references unguarded before the tag is cut.

Before tagging, verify changelog claims against reality: each named PR (#218, #222) is merged into the tagging base, the hardcoded date equals the actual release day, and the tag is cut from a commit at or after the version bump.

Do not relitigate the maintainer's patch-level bump (0.3.6→0.3.7 carrying a feature) — only a lowest-reward review raised this convention question and humans dismiss version-number pedantry on an already-decided release train.

When a docs-slimming PR deletes a section, verify the only-documented operational content — touchstone doctor, the dry-run python -m touchstone.run invocation, TOUCHSTONE_OUTPUT_DIR, .touchstone/ policy files — has a new home and name that destination (DEPLOYMENT.md, env-var table) in the flag.
Catch in-place rewrites of existing CHANGELOG bullets and require confirmation they sit under an Unreleased heading, since editing an already-published version's entry calls for a new entry instead.

After section/anchor removals, grep repo-wide (docs/, skills/, workflow comments) for stale references to #本地命令 / #规模与状态 and for old deployments that lose the Secrets→Variables migration guidance along with the deleted note.

Flag headline claims that contradict retained body text — new 'AI Committer' H1 vs advisory-only review, no-LLM gate, autonomy 默认关 — and propose a one-line disambiguating qualifier under the tagline rather than a relabel.
Flag CHANGELOG process metadata like '（用户指示）' and relative phrasing like '二次精简', insisting entries describe the change and its user impact rather than who asked or the edit sequence.

Do not fight a simplification PR over deleted philosophy/vision prose framed as lost 'safety stance' — reviewers dismiss trust-model defenses; at most request that its one operational sentence (自主边界 = 验证边界) survive as a pointer in docs/.
Do not split one section deletion into bespoke per-topic loss subtypes (operational/onboarding); report the substance once under PRA-INFO-LOSS with a concrete relocation checklist instead.

Use the canonical PRA-DANGLING-REF for orphaned anchors and lost provenance instead of bespoke renames like PRA-DOC-ORPHANED-REFERENCES, PRA-MIGRATION-NOTE-REMOVAL, or PRA-CHANGELOG-STYLE, which duplicate flags already covered by the generic types.

Emphasize spec-wording findings that name the exact patch location: push reinterpretations back to the source clause (在 §6-2 原文补注) and state the missing trigger (rebase/合并 main 后基线漂移需补一次全量), because humans apply precise one-line doc edits.
Do not relabel the drift-test finding as PRA-DRIFT-GUARD; the higher-reward review carries the identical substance under PRA-TEST, so keep the standard label and skip the exotic one.
Avoid splitting the §6-2 sync note into a separate PRA-CONSISTENCY finding; fold it into the single PRA-DOC comment instead of duplicating one doc point across two types.

Suppress speculative operational worries such as doubled polling cost or an unbounded polling loop needing a stop-loss line on pre-existing copy; humans dismiss out-of-scope behavior advice on a docs-wording PR.

Drop PRA-VERIFY demands for pre-merge proof such as a repo-wide grep evidencing the CHANGELOG completeness claim; when the docs already explain the mechanism, evidence demands read as process theater and get ignored.
Suppress hypothetical edge-case what-ifs such as unspecified sys.exit(2) watchdog classification or bool-zero codes unless an actual bug is demonstrated.
Before POSTing label creation, verify the probe failure is a true 404 and abort with a warning on 401/403 so auth or quota failures do not trigger spurious creation calls every round.
Cut per-PR API traffic by fetching the label set once and diffing locally, issuing surgical DELETEs only for labels actually present instead of guaranteed-404 deletes and redundant probes.
Do not demand stub fidelity upgrades such as fake .response objects on HTTPError; humans dismiss test-double refinement requests on already-passing suites.
Suppress demands for extra unit tests of mocked helpers (_emergency_comment env handling, never-throw guarantees) — humans consider that test-suite gold-plating on a behavior-fix PR.
Skip requests to add capsys assertions for [info] log lines; humans treat audit-trail emission nitpicks as disposable.
Do not propose refactoring tests away from private internals or centralizing label constants; humans dismiss test-style restructuring suggestions.
Do not flag hypothetical future label-name charset issues in urllib quoting; humans dismiss speculative hardening for names that do not exist.

Lead with the root-cause fix: import DEFAULT_CONTEXT_TOKENS from pr_agent_runner and interpolate it into the preflight warning via f-string instead of hardcoding '128000' again, since this literal has already drifted once (the stale 32768 text is exactly that failure).

Demand verification against pr_agent_runner.py itself — unset fallback value, whether it differs per provider/model, and whether empty or non-numeric TOUCHSTONE_LLM_CONTEXT_TOKENS takes the same path — and cite the commit where 32768 became 128000, because the diff alone never proves the number.

Require a regression test asserting check_config's warning text against the runner-imported constant (and update any existing test pinning '32768'), so the next fallback change fails a test instead of silently rotting the message.
Run a repo-wide grep for '32768' — README, SECURITY.md and ops docs, especially since the warning text itself directs readers to SECURITY/CHANGELOG — and align every stale mention in this same PR.

Verify that preflight's `if not ctx` semantics for empty-string TOUCHSTONE_LLM_CONTEXT_TOKENS match the runner's actual parsing (e.g. `os.environ.get(...) or fallback`), so the corrected message doesn't introduce a new preflight-vs-runner mismatch.

Anchor the CHANGELOG claim that the fallback '早已是 128000' to the commit or version that changed it (adding a historical entry if missing), so future drift investigations in touchstone have a traceable reference.
Don't spend a standalone finding re-explaining that 128000 is a diff budget rather than a model window — fold that clarification into the wording only if runner verification actually confirms it.

Drop changelog formatting nits (subsection placement under 未发布, placeholder-line removal, bold styling) — humans dismiss them, and they displace the behavioral checks that make a review of this literal-drift PR valuable.

Call out the fork-PR visibility asymmetry — Variables are readable in fork CI where Secrets are not, turning empty-fallback into effective values — and request a one-line changelog caveat instead of letting the blanket zero-change assertion stand.
Skip speculative changelog-date audits (year-typo guesses, timezone and ISO-style nitpicks) unless the stated date actually contradicts a known tag or merge date.
Do not pad doc-only release PRs with generic post-merge checklists (push tag v0.3.6, trigger publish pipeline, run smoke tests) that the maintainer handles mechanically at release time.
Drop the boilerplate grep-for-stale-version sweep when pyproject reads __version__ dynamically; only raise it if a hardcoded old version is actually visible in the diff.
Avoid hedged security enumerations that already concede the moved variable names look safe; either name a concrete credential-like variable or omit the concern entirely.

Run this repo's version/CHANGELOG consistency and parsing tests before merge, because the newly added [Unreleased] placeholder line and the 0.3.4-skip blockquote can break logic that assumes the first line under a heading is a regular entry.

Verify PR #214 is actually merged into main before this release commit is tagged v0.3.5, and confirm no other [Unreleased] items are silently swept into the release, so announced content matches shipped artifacts.

For the 0.3.4 number skip, confirm no v0.3.4 tag or published artifact exists anywhere, that the number is permanently retired, and that release automation assuming consecutive versions tolerates the v0.3.3→v0.3.5 jump.
Do not spend review budget on non-blocking heading rewording such as trimming the duplicated parenthetical from the ### 变更 subheading — humans dismiss cosmetic nits on release-bump PRs.
Skip prose-style rewrites of the skip note (blockquote versus declarative sentence) — reviewers dismiss wording polish that does not change meaning.
Avoid demanding pre-release build smoke checks (wheel metadata, --version output) when pyproject already reads the version dynamically — humans treat this as boilerplate verification.

Do not push for SECURITY.md edits enumerating 0.3.4's nonexistence or 0.3.3's support status on this diff, since the file is untouched here and humans dismiss cross-file scope rewrites bundled into a version bump.

Challenge blanket 'CLI 契约零变化' claims when the headline fix changes failure-path behavior: check whether a summary-comment POST failure now surfaces as a non-zero exit/loud error, and if so force the changelog to soften the claim or add an explicit behavior-change note so exit-code-dependent CI consumers don't break.

Since pyproject reads __version__ dynamically, scope the release sweep to remaining literals (README badges, SECURITY.md support table, docs, version-asserting tests) and require SECURITY.md's 0.3.2→0.3.3 truthfulness to be fixed in this same PR if it is a static list.

Stop leading with Keep-a-Changelog bottom-of-file compare-link definitions on release PRs — it appeared in every low-reward review here, so at most fold it into a one-line consistency check instead of a standalone finding.
Drop nitpicks about issue #211 being referenced in both the version heading and the 修复 subsection — redundant-issue-mention wording complaints on changelog headings get dismissed.

Don't speculate that hidden [未发布] WIP subsections were swept into 0.3.3 — the highest-reward review confirmed the header insertion moves exactly the issue-#211 bullets and leaves the placeholder, so treat the structure as correct unless the diff shows otherwise.
Suppress speculative improvement pitches like adding retry-with-backoff on the summary-comment POST; humans treat unrequested redesigns of the failure contract as noise.
Suppress verification-question findings like confirming the watchdog wraps the exact console entry point; humans expect authors to have already checked callers, and questions read as deflection.

Do not stack speculative downstream-breakage scenarios (jsonschema additionalProperties:false, strict deserialization, golden-file diffs) without evidence such consumers exist — a single concrete schema-sync note already covers the risk.

Only flag hard factual contradictions in the CHANGELOG (1239+11=1250 vs the claimed 1250→1278 jump) as a must-fix-before-release error, since release notes are audit artifacts humans actually correct.

Flag the 'zero external interface change' claim exactly once and consolidate it: documented behavior tightenings (POST retry removal, SSRF fail-closed, fail-closed diff gate) require either a narrowed claim or an upgrade-notes section.
Suppress enumeration audits over audit-item numbering (missing #44, skipped #204) — pure bookkeeping arithmetic that humans dismiss as noise.
Suppress headline-count mismatches like 'CI 三修 but only two PRs listed' — wording arithmetic with no functional consequence.
Suppress style complaints about internal IDs and symbols referenced in changelog entries — cosmetic readability nits.
Suppress speculative cross-file version-sync checks (SECURITY.md support ranges, pyproject metadata) that cannot be verified from this changelog-plus-bump diff.

Lead with the root-cause cache-starvation analysis: a near-empty pip cache entry minted on warm-hit runs can win the setup-python primary key via actions/cache first-come-first-served and permanently block the real wheel cache, so argue for disabling cache: pip on hit runs over the mkdir workaround.

Flag concrete breakage modes humans will actually fix: Linux-only pip paths and bash syntax that fail under an OS matrix or pwsh default shell, plus 2>/dev/null silently absorbing a missing python-path with no log breadcrumb or ::warning:: fallback.
Do not file a standalone PRA-RISK entry restating the empty-cache-starvation scenario already owned by the PRA-DESIGN note; duplicate framings of one mechanism read as padding.
Skip unresolvable step-id existence checks (steps.pv/steps.py) that cannot be confirmed from the diff; fold any silent-no-op concern into the design or robustness note instead.
Do not split OS-matrix portability into its own PRA-PORTABILITY finding; the macOS/Windows pip-path issue lands better as part of the single PRA-ROBUSTNESS note.
Do not critique the PR's YAML prose length or suspect date typos; comment-taste feedback is ignored when the fix itself is verified by a real run.

Insist on unit coverage of the newly-live contract ('' -> 1000, '0' -> disabled, valid int, garbage, negative) plus an end-to-end wiring self-check (set the variable to 5 and prove the gate fires), since CI changes cannot be exercised locally.

Push the operator-facing semantics — where to create the variable (repo Settings -> Actions -> Variables), the default, and the footgun that '0' disables the gate entirely — into deployment/config docs instead of leaving them as YAML comments.
Do not relabel the empty-string parse hazard as PRA-BUG-RISK; state it under PRA-CORRECTNESS, the label reviewers actually act on.
Raise malformed-variable-value concerns under PRA-ROBUSTNESS rather than PRA-VALIDATION, which reviewers read as duplicate noise.

Lead every docs-only PR review with the parity check: this README documents comment folding, the L1/L2/L3 gate, and multi-round polling with zero code in the diff, so demand links to the merged implementing PRs or verification that each behavior exists on main before anything else.

Treat the dropped stop-line as an agent-safety bug, not a docs nit: the README's condensed polling instruction has no max rounds, timeout, or backoff, so literal agents loop forever hammering the GitHub API.

Hold the round-detection rule to implementable-spec standards: pin the created_at comparison baseline, name which Touchstone comment kind counts as the round signal, and state the never-edit-in-place invariant the rule depends on.

Demand the L2 gate's edge behavior in writing: '<!--' inside a validated marker's JSON payload, HTML-comment examples inside fenced code blocks, and nested '-->' will be corrupted by mechanical neutralization, so the doc must either exempt or own these cases.

Skip self-labeled 'Minor' annotation-sync notes like tree annotation vs numbered-step narrative: they read as filler and drag review quality down without changing any decision.

Suppress generic 'also update the honesty/boundary section' asks: unless they name the specific new failure modes (GraphQL fold permissions, neutralization altering report text, polling burden) they read as boilerplate and go unactioned.
Suppress generic test-polish suggestions (idempotence assertions, brittle-source-sentinel critiques) when no failing behavior is demonstrated.
Demand idempotency: an already-collapsed comment must be skipped via a sentinel so the loop does not re-PATCH every round, burning quota and spamming edit history.

Suppress missing-implementation alarms that stem from truncated diffs; only raise them when the referenced symbols are verifiably absent from the repo, not the diff view.

Report only demonstrable runtime breakage — e.g. verify that cross-module references like `_checklist` in touchstone/loop.py and `checklist_mod` in orchestrator.py resolve to real imports and flag a NameError only when the symbol is genuinely unresolvable post-merge.

When a change reduces a test to pinning a constant, rename or re-document it so its stated purpose matches what it now actually asserts (anti-regression, not layout coverage).
Do not propose consolidating overlapping tests or extracting shared parsing helpers, since humans dismiss structural refactoring suggestions when the change only deletes code.

Flag monkeypatching of the private render._ack_skill_path and push for a public injection seam (a skill_path parameter on render_reference or an env var), since reviewers at every reward tier converged on this coupling.

Do not use PRA-REGRESSION-RISK; fold the grep-for-leftovers point into PRA-LEFTOVER so it lands as one concrete checklist.

Do not mint PRA-DATA-INTEGRITY for provenance loss on deletions; raise soft-delete and archive guidance as PRA-PREVENT or PRA-ROBUSTNESS, since novel types appeared only in the worst-scoring review.
Do not emit PRA-VERIFIABILITY for claims that are asserted but not demonstrated; route that demand into PRA-CORRECTNESS or PRA-COMPLETENESS, where high-reward reviews place it.
